title: Poll: Pan Pacs Expected to Be Speed Central of 2026 Swimming Season
summary: With no Olympics or World Championships on the 2026 calendar, the summer's elite swimming is scattered across four major meets: the Commonwealth Games, Pan Pacific Championships, European Championships, and Asian Games. So which one will crown the most event winners with the year's fastest times? SwimSwam readers have spoken—and they're betting big on Pan Pacs. In our latest A3 Performance Poll, a commanding 59.8% of respondents chose the Pan Pacific Championships, held this August in Australia. The European Championships trailed at 24.3%, while the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games garnered just 9% and 6.9%, respectively. The rationale is clear: the women's field at Pan Pacs is absurdly deep. At the 2025 World Championships, 14 of 17 individual female gold medalists hailed from core Pan Pac nations—the USA, Australia, and Canada. That trend has continued this season, with 12 of the 17 top-ranked women coming from those countries. The ace in the hole? Canadian phenom Summer McIntosh, the world's most dominant female swimmer, will race only at Pan Pacs, skipping the Commonwealth Games. Australian stars Cameron McEvoy, Kyle Chalmers, and Shayna Jack are also prioritizing Pan Pacs. On the men's side, the picture is murkier. European swimmers own eight of the fastest times this season, while Pan Pac countries claim just two world-leading marks—both from Australian Sam Short. But polls aren't just about current rankings; they're about potential. Swimmers like Kaylee McKeown and David Popovici haven't posted world-leaders yet but could easily do so when rested and tapered. As one reader commented, "Pan Pacs has the star power and the depth. When the pressure's on, that's where the fireworks will be." So mark your calendars: if you want to see the year's swiftest swims, the Pan Pacific pool is the place to be.
why_it_matters: For young fans and athletes, the poll highlights how sports seasons without a single unifying championship can shift excitement and talent toward different stages; understanding this teaches how the sports calendar influences where history gets made.

background_read: In 2026 there is no Olympic Games or FINA World Championships, so the top events are the Pan Pacific Championships (for nations like USA, Australia, Canada, Japan), the European Championships, the Commonwealth Games (for countries mostly from the former British Empire), and the Asian Games.
Summer McIntosh (Canada) is a teenage swimming sensation who won multiple gold medals at the 2024 Olympics and 2025 World Championships, making her one of the most dominant athletes in the pool.

Kyle Chalmers (Australia) is an Olympic gold medalist in the 100m freestyle, and Kaylee McKeown (Australia) holds world records in backstroke. David Popovici (Romania) is a young freestyle star who burst onto the scene with world records as a teenager.

SwimSwam is a leading swimming news site that often runs polls among its readers, who are usually dedicated fans, coaches, and athletes, so the results reflect informed opinions rather than a random sample.

└─ Poll result: 59.8% Pan Pacs, 24.3% Europeans, 9% Commonwealth, 6.9% Asian Games
MAIN ARGUMENT: The women's depth at Pan Pacs is overwhelming
├─ EVIDENCE A: 14 of 17 individual female gold medals at 2025 Worlds went to Pan Pac nations
├─ EVIDENCE B: 12 of 17 top-ranked women this season are from USA, Australia, Canada
└─ EVIDENCE C: Summer McIntosh (world's most dominant female) is skipping Commonwealth Games
SECONDARY POINT: Men's side is less clear
├─ European men hold 8 of the fastest times this season
└─ Pan Pac men have only two world-leading marks (both from Sam Short)
COUNTERPOINT: Polls are about potential, not just current stats
└─ Stars like McKeown and Popovici haven't posted leaders yet but could when rested and tapered
CONCLUSION: The reader quote reinforces that star power and depth will create the year's swiftest swims.

perspectives.perspective: Positive – opportunity for Pan Pac nations to shine
perspectives.description: With no global championship, the Pan Pacific meet becomes the de facto summit for the sport's best female swimmers. Host nation Australia and stars like McIntosh get a home-turf spotlight that could launch the next wave of inspiration.

perspectives.perspective: Negative / critical – European talent might be undervalued
perspectives.description: The poll may underrate European men's depth, as their eight world-leading times suggest they could dominate their own championships. Tapering changes everything, so writing off Europeans too early could be a mistake.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral / analytical – the role of meet distribution in non-Olympic years
perspectives.description: When the swimming calendar is fragmented, different athletes choose different priorities. McIntosh's decision to skip the Commonwealth Games is strategic, and such choices will increasingly shape which records fall at which meets.

If rested stars deliver fireworks at Pan Pacs, the event could rival a World Championships in public attention. This might push swimming's governing bodies to reconsider how they schedule major events to avoid watering down competition in non-Olympic years.
